# External Agents for Entire CLI

This repository contains standalone external agent binaries that extend the [Entire CLI](https://github.com/entireio/cli) with support for additional AI coding agents.

## What Are External Agents?

External agents are standalone binaries (named `entire-agent-<name>`) that teach Entire CLI how to work with AI coding agents it doesn't natively support. When an external agent is installed on your `PATH`, Entire discovers it automatically and gains the ability to:

- **Create checkpoints** during AI coding sessions so you can rewind mistakes
- **Capture transcripts** of what the AI agent did and why
- **Install hooks** so the AI agent's lifecycle events (start, stop, commit) flow through Entire

External agents communicate with Entire CLI via subcommands that accept and return JSON over stdin/stdout. See the [external agent protocol spec](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md) for the full interface.

## Available Agents

| Agent | Directory | Status |
|-------|-----------|--------|
| [Kiro](agents/entire-agent-kiro/) | `agents/entire-agent-kiro/` | Implemented — hooks + transcript analysis |
| [Amp](agents/entire-agent-amp/) | `agents/entire-agent-amp/` | Implemented — hooks + transcript analysis + token calculation + compact transcripts |
| [LangGraph](agents/entire-agent-langgraph/) | `agents/entire-agent-langgraph/` | Implemented — Python callback bridge + transcript analysis |
| [CrewAI](agents/entire-agent-crewai/) | `agents/entire-agent-crewai/` | Implemented — Python event listener bridge + transcript analysis |
| [Qwen Code](agents/entire-agent-qwen/) | `agents/entire-agent-qwen/` | Implemented — hooks + transcript analysis + compact transcripts |
| [Grok Build](agents/entire-agent-grok/) | `agents/entire-agent-grok/` | Implemented — hooks + transcript analysis + compact transcripts |
| [Oh My Pi](agents/entire-agent-omp/) | `agents/entire-agent-omp/` | Implemented — hooks + transcript analysis + compact transcripts |
| [Kilo](agents/entire-agent-kilo/) | `agents/entire-agent-kilo/` | Implemented (preview) — hooks + transcript analysis + token calculation + compact transcripts |
| [Goose](agents/entire-agent-goose/) | `agents/entire-agent-goose/` | Implemented (preview) — hooks + transcript analysis + token calculation + compact transcripts |
| [Hermes Agent](agents/entire-agent-hermes/) | `agents/entire-agent-hermes/` | Implemented (preview) — sanitized observer hooks + transcript analysis + compact transcripts |

See each agent's own README for setup and usage instructions.

## Enabling External Agents

External agent discovery is opt-in. Once an `entire-agent-<name>` binary is on your `PATH`, set `external_agents: true` in the repo's `.entire/settings.json` so Entire scans for it:

```json
{
  "external_agents": true
}
```

Without this flag, Entire ignores external agent binaries even when they're installed.

### LangGraph and CrewAI

LangGraph and CrewAI support is provided by the Python package
[`entire-adapter`](https://pypi.org/project/entire-adapter/). These entries
bridge framework lifecycle callbacks into Entire rather than wrapping a
standalone chat CLI.

For LangGraph or LangChain projects:

```bash
pip install "entire-adapter[langgraph]"
entire enable --agent langgraph --telemetry=false
```

For CrewAI projects:

```bash
pip install "entire-adapter[crewai]"
entire enable --agent crewai --telemetry=false
```

After enabling, add the adapter to your framework code. LangGraph uses
`EntireCallbackHandler`; CrewAI uses `EntireCrewAIListener`.

### Qwen Code

Qwen support targets the terminal `qwen` coding agent:

```bash
cd agents/entire-agent-qwen
mise run build
cp entire-agent-qwen /usr/local/bin/

cd /path/to/your/repo
entire enable --agent qwen --telemetry=false
qwen -p "Create hello.txt with hello world" --yolo
```

The adapter installs Qwen command hooks in `.qwen/settings.json`. The stable Entire sidecar transcript lives in a repo-scoped OS temp directory, with a small `.entire/tmp/<session>.json` marker for Entire session discovery. Qwen Code must execute actual tools for checkpoints; local model backends that only print XML-style tool tags as text will not fire Qwen `PostToolUse` hooks.

### Grok Build

Grok support targets the Grok Build CLI:

```bash
cd agents/entire-agent-grok
mise run build
cp entire-agent-grok ~/.local/bin/

cd /path/to/your/repo
entire enable --agent grok --telemetry=false
grok "Create hello.txt with hello world"
```

The adapter installs Grok command hooks in `.grok/hooks/entire.json` and reads native transcripts from `~/.grok/sessions/<encoded-cwd>/<session-id>/chat_history.jsonl`. Project hooks require folder trust (`/hooks-trust` or `--trust`) before they execute, and until the folder is trusted Grok skips them silently, so nothing is captured.

Restored sessions can be resumed with `grok --resume <session-id>`, but not at full fidelity: Grok's `encrypted_content` reasoning state is stripped before storage, so a resumed session replays the conversation without its prior reasoning context. Sessions captured before this behaviour shipped cannot be resumed at all. See the [agent README](agents/entire-agent-grok/README.md#session-restore-and-resume).

### Hermes Agent

Hermes support uses an embedded standalone observer plugin and requires an explicit `HERMES_HOME`; it never falls back to the default profile. The observer stores a repository-scoped sanitized JSONL transcript and intentionally excludes system/developer prompts, memory, full history, platform identifiers, environment data, secrets, tool arguments, and raw tool results.

```bash
cd agents/entire-agent-hermes
mise run build
export PATH="$PWD:$PATH"
export HERMES_HOME=/absolute/path/to/a/hermes/profile

cd /path/to/your/repo
entire enable --agent hermes --telemetry=false
hermes --yolo --ignore-rules -z "Create hello.txt with hello world"
```

One profile can register multiple repositories. Uninstalling the adapter from one repository leaves unrelated Hermes plugins and other repository registrations intact. See the [Hermes adapter README](agents/entire-agent-hermes/) for the disposable-profile verification flow.

## Building a New External Agent

This repo includes a skill that guides you through building a new external agent with two test layers:

1. **Protocol compliance** — generic subcommand coverage from [`entireio/external-agents-tests`](https://github.com/entireio/external-agents-tests)
2. **Lifecycle integration** — repo-local `e2e/` tests that exercise `entire enable`, prompt execution, checkpoints, and rewind
3. **Implementation** — build the binary until both layers pass, then add unit tests

### Getting Started — Zero Setup

Clone the repo and open it in your AI coding tool. Each tool auto-discovers the skill with no additional configuration:

| Tool | How it discovers | What to say |
|------|-----------------|-------------|
| **Claude Code** | `.claude/skills/` directory | `/entire-external-agent` |
| **Codex** | `AGENTS.md` at project root | "Build an external agent" |
| **Cursor** | `.cursor/rules/` directory | "Build an external agent" |
| **OpenCode** | `.opencode/plugins/` auto-loaded | "Build an external agent" |

The skill files live in `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/` if you want to read the details.

## Testing

Testing is intentionally split:

- **Generic protocol checks** run in GitHub Actions via [`entireio/external-agents-tests`](https://github.com/entireio/external-agents-tests). The workflow builds each `entire-agent-*` binary in this repo and runs the shared compliance suite against it.
- **Agent unit/build checks** run in GitHub Actions for every `agents/entire-agent-*` directory discovered at runtime.
- **Lifecycle tests** stay in this repo's [`e2e/`](e2e/) harness. These verify the parts that depend on Entire itself and on the real agent CLI: prompt execution, hook installation after `entire enable`, checkpoint creation, rewind behavior, and interactive sessions.
- **Unit tests** live with each agent implementation under [`agents/`](agents/).

### Running Tests

```bash
# Run default test suite for all agents
mise run test

# Same as test, kept for explicit CI-style naming
mise run test:ci

# Run lifecycle integration tests from this repo
mise run test:e2e

# Same as test:e2e, kept as the explicit name
mise run test:e2e:lifecycle
```

Protocol compliance runs in CI through [`.github/workflows/protocol-compliance.yml`](.github/workflows/protocol-compliance.yml).

For a newly added agent to be picked up automatically by local root tasks and CI, add `agents/entire-agent-<name>/mise.toml` with `build` and `test` tasks. The shared runner falls back to Go defaults when `go.mod` exists, but the `mise` tasks are the contract for non-standard setups.

### Lifecycle Harness Architecture

The lifecycle harness auto-discovers and builds all agents in `agents/` via `TestMain`:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `e2e/setup_test.go` | `TestMain` entry point — discovers agents, builds binaries, configures PATH |
| `e2e/lifecycle_test.go` | Shared lifecycle scenarios run against every registered agent |
| `e2e/agents/` | Agent adapters for the real CLIs used during lifecycle tests |
| `e2e/entire/` | Entire CLI wrappers used by lifecycle assertions |
| `e2e/testutil/` | Repo setup, artifact capture, git helpers, and checkpoint assertions |

### Environment Variables

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN` | Path to the `entire` binary (defaults to `entire` from PATH) |
| `E2E_AGENT` | Filter lifecycle runs to a single registered agent |
| `E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR` | Override lifecycle artifact output directory |
| `E2E_KEEP_REPOS` | Preserve temp repos for debugging |
| `E2E_CONCURRENT_TEST_LIMIT` | Override the per-agent lifecycle concurrency limit |
| `QWEN_E2E` | Set to `1` with `E2E_AGENT=qwen` to run live Qwen Code lifecycle tests |
| `HERMES_E2E` | Set to `1` with `E2E_AGENT=hermes` and an explicit disposable `HERMES_HOME` to run live Hermes lifecycle tests |

## Repository Layout

```
agents/                          # Standalone external agent projects
  entire-agent-kiro/             # Kiro agent (Go binary)
  entire-agent-amp/              # Amp agent (Go binary)
  entire-agent-langgraph/        # LangGraph callback bridge (Python wrapper)
  entire-agent-crewai/           # CrewAI listener bridge (Python wrapper)
  entire-agent-qwen/             # Qwen Code agent (Go binary)
  entire-agent-omp/              # Oh My Pi agent (Go binary)
  entire-agent-kilo/             # Kilo agent (Go binary)
  entire-agent-hermes/           # Hermes Agent (Go binary + embedded observer plugin)
e2e/                             # Lifecycle integration harness
.github/workflows/               # CI, including protocol compliance via external-agents-tests
.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/  # Skill files (research, test-writer, implementer)
AGENTS.md                        # Codex auto-discovery
.cursor/rules/                   # Cursor auto-discovery
.opencode/plugins/               # OpenCode auto-discovery
```

    steps:

            name="$(basename "$dir")"
            if [[ -n "$entries" ]]; then
              entries="${entries},"

            entries="${entries}{\"name\":\"${name}\",\"dir\":\"${dir}\",\"binary\":\"${dir}/${name}\"}"

# Entire Adapter

Python adapter that lets LangGraph/LangChain and CrewAI agents participate in Entire checkpoint tracking.

It provides:

- `EntireCallbackHandler` for LangChain and LangGraph callback configs.
- `EntireCrewAIListener` for CrewAI's event bus.
- Three Entire external-agent binaries:
  - `entire-agent-langgraph`
  - `entire-agent-crewai`
  - `entire-agent-entire-adapter` for backward-compatible generic use.

## Why

Custom Python agents often edit files through tools, but their prompt/tool context is easy to lose once the final Git diff lands. Entire Adapter maps framework lifecycle events to Entire hooks so commits can be linked to agent sessions, tool calls, and checkpoint history.

## Install

For LangGraph/LangChain:

```bash
pip install "entire-adapter[langgraph]"
entire enable --agent langgraph --telemetry=false
```

For CrewAI:

```bash
pip install "entire-adapter[crewai]"
entire enable --agent crewai --telemetry=false

item.stdout:
# Security Policy

We take security seriously at Entire. We appreciate your efforts to responsibly disclose vulnerabilities and will make every effort to acknowledge your contributions.

## Reporting a Vulnerability

**Please do not report security vulnerabilities through public GitHub issues.**

Instead, please send security-related reports to **[security@entire.io](mailto:security@entire.io)**.

### What to Include

When reporting a vulnerability, please include:

1. **Description** - A clear description of the vulnerability
2. **Impact** - What an attacker could achieve by exploiting this issue
3. **Steps to reproduce** - Detailed steps to reproduce the vulnerability
4. **Affected versions** - Which versions of the CLI are affected (if known)
5. **Suggested fix** - If you have ideas on how to fix it (optional)

### What to Expect

- **Acknowledgment** - We will acknowledge receipt of your report within 48 hours
- **Updates** - We will keep you informed of our progress as we investigate
- **Resolution** - We aim to resolve critical vulnerabilities within 90 days

## Confidentiality

**All reports will be kept confidential.** We will not share your information with third parties without your consent, except as required by law.

## Supported Versions

We recommend always running the latest version of the Entire CLI.

## Scope

This security policy applies to:

- The Entire CLI (`entire` command-line tool)
- Official Entire GitHub repositories
- Entire-related services at entire.com or entire.io

### Out of Scope

The following are generally not considered security vulnerabilities:

- Issues in third-party dependencies (please report these upstream)
- Social engineering attacks
- Denial of service attacks
- Issues requiring physical access to a user's device

---

## Security Advisories

Security advisories are issued when a confirmed vulnerability can be exploited by a remote or non-local actor. Because the Entire CLI is primarily used as a local development tool, the following are generally treated as **bug reports rather than security advisories**:

- Regular expression performance issues (ReDoS) that only affect local execution
- Resource exhaustion that requires local access to trigger
- Issues that cannot be exploited without direct access to the user's machine

Use GitHub Issues for the respective repository to report bugs.

---

Thank you for helping keep Entire and our community safe!

57b275ac6 2026-09-01T11:52:52+01:00 agent: reject volume-relative paths in SessionStore.Name
Cursor Bugbot, session_store.go:146 (High). Not in the trail findings.

Name gated only on filepath.IsAbs, so a Windows drive-relative path such as
"C:foo" — separator-free, and reported non-absolute — was accepted as a name
inside the store, while filepath.Join drops the base directory when the
appended element carries a volume. SessionFile then handed that escaped path
back as absPath.

validation.ValidateSessionID already rejects this shape, and its comment
describes the same mechanism, so the reachable paths are covered today. But
SessionStore is the containment layer this branch introduces — Name exists to
answer "is this inside the store?" independently of whether a caller
remembered to validate — and it was the one place pairing IsAbs with nothing.
The other three (ValidateSessionID, alternates_fs, alternates_rewrite) all
pair it with VolumeName.

Route a volumed path down the absolute branch so filepath.Rel rejects it
across volumes. No-op on Unix, where VolumeName is always empty.

Not verified on Windows hardware: the change is inert on this platform, and
CI's Windows leg only runs tests matching (Windows|MSYS).

83677f751 2026-09-01T11:52:47+01:00 Pin every path component instead of checking it and looking again
NoSymlinkedParent walked a name's parents with Lstat and then handed the
WHOLE name back to the original root, so the thing that was checked and
the thing that was opened were resolved twice, independently. Everything
in this package now opens each component in turn, keeps the descriptor,
and operates relative to it: OpenDirNoSymlinks descends one component at
a time, OpenParentNoSymlinks pins the parent and returns the leaf, and
ReadFileNoFollow, OpenFileNoFollow, LstatNoSymlinks, RemoveNoSymlinks,
ReadDirNoSymlinks and WalkDirNoSymlinks are all expressed on top of that
pair. NoSymlinkedParent survives as a predicate and now says in its own
doc that a caller acting on the result must re-open through
OpenParentNoSymlinks rather than trust it.

MkdirAllNoSymlink follows the same rule for the directories it creates,
so a component that appears between the check and the Mkdir is opened
and identity-checked like any other rather than being MkdirAll'd blind.
OpenChild stops reporting a regular file as ErrSymlinkedPath and returns
ErrWalkRootNotDirectory: replacing a link and replacing a file are
different remedies.

The atomic writers no longer fsync. The rename is what gives every
caller here the property it actually needs, that a reader never sees a
torn file; fsync buys durability across a power loss, and nothing
written through these functions is worth that — settings, session state,
caches and manifests are all reconstructible. It is not free either,
measured at 14x on a 4KiB payload (1.02ms against 71µs) with session
state written on every agent hook. What is surrendered is stated in the
doc rather than left implicit.

Writing atomically into an agent's config directory does leave a temp
file beside the target if the process dies between the create and the
rename. The window is now a few tens of microseconds and only `enable`
and `trail checkout` can open it, but the result is permanent, and
Entire diffs untracked files across a turn — so a months-old
.claude/settings.json.<hex>.tmp gets captured into the next checkpoint
as a file that turn created. `entire clean --all` now sweeps them. The
capture path deliberately does NOT learn to ignore them: the worktree
belongs to the user, and silently dropping a file from their checkpoint
is worse than the stray it would hide.

HookConfigFile now refuses a symlinked leaf as well as a symlinked
parent, reversing an earlier decision in this branch. The reason is
recorded where the policy is: the merge read pulls the link target's
contents into what Entire writes, and the write is a rename, so it
replaces the user's link with a regular file rather than following it.
Both are silent. A deliberately symlinked settings.json still works by
keeping it out of the index, which is what a dotfile workflow does.

331c7b130 2026-09-01T11:52:44+01:00 Refuse what os.Root only confined
The anchors landed in the previous three commits. This is the tail, and
most of it is one bug wearing several hats: os.Root contains a path
without saying anything about what the path is.

fs.WalkDir takes its walk root's DirEntry from fs.Stat, which follows a
symlink, and only the entries below it from ReadDir, which does not.
Every symlink guard here inspected d.Type() inside the callback, so none
of them covered the root: a symlinked .entire/metadata/<session> was
descended into and its target redacted, committed and pushed.
filepath.Walk lstat'd its root, so this was lost in the conversion, not
absent from the start. osroot.WalkDirNoSymlinks lstats the root and
refuses a symlink at both levels; the two checkpoint metadata walks,
clean's tmp walk and doctor's reporter use it. redact.LoadPacks gets the
same check through fs.ReadLinkFS, which os.Root.FS() implements, so it
keeps its fs.FS-only API and its dependency-free position. A symlinked
.entire is refused rather than followed now, so doctor and CLAUDE.md stop
telling the user that intentional setups keep working.

jsonutil.WriteFileAtomicIn leaves <base>.<16 hex>.tmp beside its target,
and .entire/metadata/<session> is copied wholesale into every checkpoint
tree. A hook killed between the create and the rename left an orphan that
was committed on every checkpoint from then on, and ParseChunkIndex read
it back as a transcript CHUNK: fmt.Sscanf("%03d") stops at the first
non-digit, so full.jsonl.123abc...tmp parsed as chunk 123 and was
reassembled into the transcript. Both walks skip jsonutil.IsTempName, and
a chunk suffix must now be entirely digits.

SessionStore resolved its root through osroot.Shared, a registry that
never evicts. searchTranscriptInProjectDirs opens a store for every
candidate directory it walks under an agent's session base dir, so each
probe retained a directory fd for the life of the process, measured at
one per directory against zero for the os.Stat it replaced. A store is
not a long-lived anchor: it opens a root per operation and closes it
again. plugin_install_remote took a shared root on a staging directory it
then RemoveAll'd, with no Forget.

Smaller, same theme: createBlobFromFile read WORKTREE files through
entiredir, binding them to .entire's policy; removeEntireDirectory
guessed cwd for a recursive delete on any WorktreeRoot failure rather
than only on git's positive not-a-repository verdict; the session-state
read path opened a child root with no symlink check, which
osroot.OpenChild now performs; and settings.readConfinedIn was a second
copy of osroot.OpenNoFollow.

The external-agent discovery tests built a fake .git directory and leaned
on settings.Load falling back to a cwd-relative path when the anchor
failed. That fallback is gone, so they name the worktree root in the
context instead. One of them was passing for the wrong reason: a disabled
setting and an unreadable one both end at IsExternalAgentsEnabled
returning false.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M14ZJ70AXMSM9M2WBNSDG95G

8057a0ef9 2026-09-01T11:52:42+01:00 Anchor every os.Root on a trusted base
An os.Root is only as trustworthy as the directory it is opened on, and the
wrong version of that reads as the right one:

    root, _ := osroot.Shared(filepath.Dir(target))
    data, _ := osroot.ReadFile(root, filepath.Base(target))

Every component the caller resolved sits ABOVE that root, so the containment
covers one fixed name and enforces nothing the filepath.Join had not already
decided. A symlink at .claude, at .entire, at entire-investigations is
resolved before the root exists. Anchoring one level up -- on a directory a
resolver produced -- makes those components names INSIDE the root, which is
what os.Root and MkdirAllNoSymlink can refuse.

Three call sites shipped the derived-base shape, and one of them had a
containment check that could never fire: settings.clonePreferencesRoot
computed its common dir as filepath.Dir(filepath.Dir(abs)) and handed both
to gitdir.OpenPathIn, so the relative path was correct by construction. It
now recovers the common dir by removing a compile-time constant suffix,
which fails loudly on a path of the wrong shape. contexts and discovery take
the DIRECTORY the caller chose instead of the file: configRoot(configDir),
and a cacheFile{dir, name} pair in place of a joined path.

Two roots stay anchored on their target's parent and now say why: tokenstore
($ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE_PATH) and settings' explicit-path fallback both act on
a path the CALLER named, so its parent is the caller's choice too and there
is no separate trusted base to prefer.

The seven agent hook-config trees had no root at all. Each of .claude,
.cursor, .gemini, .github/hooks, .factory, .codex and .opencode/plugin was
four lines of filepath.Join + os.MkdirAll + os.WriteFile carrying a
//nolint:gosec saying the path came from the repo root -- which describes
where the path was BUILT, not where it RESOLVES. A working tree arrives by
clone, so a repository carrying a checked-in symlink at .claude had `entire
enable` create directories and write JSON through it, outside the repository
included. agent.HookConfigFile replaces all seven with one type anchored on
the worktree root.

One behaviour change falls out of that and is pinned by a test rather than
left to be discovered: an ABSOLUTE symlink at the config FILE
(.claude/settings.json -> ~/dotfiles/...) no longer resolves, because
os.Root refuses absolute symlinks unconditionally. A relative link inside
the worktree still works, and a symlinked config DIRECTORY is now refused --
which is the point.

investigate gets the same treatment, and there it covers a sink its own
comments already warned about: StateStore.RunDir noted that an unvalidated
run id "would be a path-traversal sink" because callers feed the result to
os.RemoveAll, and clean did exactly that with two functions returning
absolute paths. Deleting now belongs to the stores, which resolve a run id
as a name inside the git common dir. Reading gets it too, closing a real
gap: LocalManifest.FindingsDoc is an absolute path decoded from a JSON file
on disk, and show plus the run footer both followed it, so a manifest could
choose which file was printed. Bootstrap no longer writes at all -- it
renders a body the caller persists through StateStore.WriteFindings.

Also rooted: the checkpoint loose-object delete; the trail worktree
checkout's .gitignore and .worktreeinclude, plus the SOURCE half of its
ignored-file copy (the destination was already rooted on the argument that
the branch content is not user-authored -- the same argument applies to the
files being read); the plugin asset download; the hook-path attribution
read, which read every file in `git status` output on a joined path; the
trail-review location reads, which went through a hand-rolled validator and
take their path from the API; and rewind's restore, which kept a
`repoRoot = "."` fallback and its own os.OpenRoot. Restoring a checkpoint
tree into whatever directory the process is sitting in is worse than not
restoring; it now fails, goes through worktreedir, and creates directories
with MkdirAllNoSymlink, which matters most there because the tree entries
may have been fetched from a remote.

agent.sessionStoreForWrite had the inverse problem: a SessionRef outside the
agent's session store fell through to a root anchored on its own parent, so
the one input that failed the containment check was the one input that
disabled it. The comment justifying that said some agents resolve a restored
session to a sibling directory; they do not -- Codex's
ResolveRestoredSessionFile nests inside the store -- so the branch was
unreachable as well as unsound. It is an error now.

fdff08c9d 2026-06-04T16:24:32+02:00 harden: address PR review — Windows volume + glob-metachar session IDs
Three issues from PR #1365 review:

- ValidateSessionID accepted Windows drive-relative paths ("C:foo"):
  separator-free and not reported absolute by filepath.IsAbs, yet
  filepath.Join drops the base dir on a volume name. Reject ":" (the
  volume separator) — portable and testable; no legitimate session ID
  contains a colon.

- ValidateSessionID accepted glob metacharacters ("*", "?", "["). Session
  IDs are interpolated into filepath.Glob patterns (agent transcript
  lookup in gemini/pi/codex, session-state cleanup), so a "*" could match
  unrelated files. Reject them at the validator choke point.

- StateStore.Clear and ClearSessionState globbed "<sessionID>.*" to find
  files to DELETE. With the permissive validator a session ID of "*"
  would have matched and removed every session's state (DoS/data-loss
  within the state dir). Replace globbing with literal prefix matching so
  deletion can never depend on pattern interpretation, even if a future
  caller skips validation.

Adds regression tests for the drive-relative and glob-metacharacter cases.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: ed740e10abe5

71790eaa8 2026-06-04T12:16:18+02:00 harden: reject ".", "..", and absolute paths in ValidateSessionID
ValidateSessionID previously rejected only path separators and empty
input. A bare "." or ".." is separator-free yet still traverses when an
agent uses the ID as a path segment (e.g. Copilot CLI builds
<dir>/<id>/events.jsonl), and the separator check can miss
platform-specific absolute forms (Windows drive paths). Reject both.

Because the same validator guards both checkpoint writes and the
resume/rewind restore boundaries, this tightens the whole class without
affecting UUID-style IDs.

//nolint:gosec saying the path came from the repo root -- which describes

the worktree still works, and a symlinked config DIRECTORY is now refused --
which is the point.

renders a body the caller persists through StateStore.WriteFindings.

Three issues from PR #1365 review:

  separator-free and not reported absolute by filepath.IsAbs, yet
  filepath.Join drops the base dir on a volume name. Reject ":" (the
  volume separator) — portable and testable; no legitimate session ID
  contains a colon.

  files to DELETE. With the permissive validator a session ID of "*"
  would have matched and removed every session's state (DoS/data-loss
  within the state dir). Replace globbing with literal prefix matching so
  deletion can never depend on pattern interpretation, even if a future
  caller skips validation.

71790eaa8 2026-06-04T12:16:18+02:00 harden: reject ".", "..", and absolute paths in ValidateSessionID

input. A bare "." or ".." is separator-free yet still traverses when an
agent uses the ID as a path segment (e.g. Copilot CLI builds
<dir>/<id>/events.jsonl), and the separator check can miss
platform-specific absolute forms (Windows drive paths). Reject both.

resume/rewind restore boundaries, this tightens the whole class without
affecting UUID-style IDs.

83677f751 2026-09-01T11:52:47+01:00 Pin every path component instead of checking it and looking again
NoSymlinkedParent walked a name's parents with Lstat and then handed the
WHOLE name back to the original root, so the thing that was checked and
the thing that was opened were resolved twice, independently. Everything
in this package now opens each component in turn, keeps the descriptor,
and operates relative to it: OpenDirNoSymlinks descends one component at
a time, OpenParentNoSymlinks pins the parent and returns the leaf, and
ReadFileNoFollow, OpenFileNoFollow, LstatNoSymlinks, RemoveNoSymlinks,
ReadDirNoSymlinks and WalkDirNoSymlinks are all expressed on top of that
pair. NoSymlinkedParent survives as a predicate and now says in its own
doc that a caller acting on the result must re-open through
OpenParentNoSymlinks rather than trust it.

MkdirAllNoSymlink follows the same rule for the directories it creates,
so a component that appears between the check and the Mkdir is opened
and identity-checked like any other rather than being MkdirAll'd blind.
OpenChild stops reporting a regular file as ErrSymlinkedPath and returns
ErrWalkRootNotDirectory: replacing a link and replacing a file are
different remedies.

The atomic writers no longer fsync. The rename is what gives every
caller here the property it actually needs, that a reader never sees a
torn file; fsync buys durability across a power loss, and nothing
written through these functions is worth that — settings, session state,
caches and manifests are all reconstructible. It is not free either,
measured at 14x on a 4KiB payload (1.02ms against 71µs) with session
state written on every agent hook. What is surrendered is stated in the
doc rather than left implicit.

Writing atomically into an agent's config directory does leave a temp
file beside the target if the process dies between the create and the
rename. The window is now a few tens of microseconds and only `enable`
and `trail checkout` can open it, but the result is permanent, and
Entire diffs untracked files across a turn — so a months-old
.claude/settings.json.<hex>.tmp gets captured into the next checkpoint
as a file that turn created. `entire clean --all` now sweeps them. The
capture path deliberately does NOT learn to ignore them: the worktree
belongs to the user, and silently dropping a file from their checkpoint
is worse than the stray it would hide.

HookConfigFile now refuses a symlinked leaf as well as a symlinked
parent, reversing an earlier decision in this branch. The reason is
recorded where the policy is: the merge read pulls the link target's
contents into what Entire writes, and the write is a rename, so it
replaces the user's link with a regular file rather than following it.
Both are silent. A deliberately symlinked settings.json still works by
keeping it out of the index, which is what a dotfile workflow does.

The anchors landed in the previous three commits. This is the tail, and
most of it is one bug wearing several hats: os.Root contains a path
without saying anything about what the path is.

fs.WalkDir takes its walk root's DirEntry from fs.Stat, which follows a
symlink, and only the entries below it from ReadDir, which does not.
Every symlink guard here inspected d.Type() inside the callback, so none
of them covered the root: a symlinked .entire/metadata/<session> was
descended into and its target redacted, committed and pushed.
filepath.Walk lstat'd its root, so this was lost in the conversion, not
absent from the start. osroot.WalkDirNoSymlinks lstats the root and
refuses a symlink at both levels; the two checkpoint metadata walks,
clean's tmp walk and doctor's reporter use it. redact.LoadPacks gets the
same check through fs.ReadLinkFS, which os.Root.FS() implements, so it
keeps its fs.FS-only API and its dependency-free position. A symlinked
.entire is refused rather than followed now, so doctor and CLAUDE.md stop
telling the user that intentional setups keep working.

jsonutil.WriteFileAtomicIn leaves <base>.<16 hex>.tmp beside its target,
and .entire/metadata/<session> is copied wholesale into every checkpoint
tree. A hook killed between the create and the rename left an orphan that
was committed on every checkpoint from then on, and ParseChunkIndex read
it back as a transcript CHUNK: fmt.Sscanf("%03d") stops at the first
non-digit, so full.jsonl.123abc...tmp parsed as chunk 123 and was
reassembled into the transcript. Both walks skip jsonutil.IsTempName, and
a chunk suffix must now be entirely digits.

SessionStore resolved its root through osroot.Shared, a registry that
never evicts. searchTranscriptInProjectDirs opens a store for every
candidate directory it walks under an agent's session base dir, so each
probe retained a directory fd for the life of the process, measured at
one per directory against zero for the os.Stat it replaced. A store is
not a long-lived anchor: it opens a root per operation and closes it
again. plugin_install_remote took a shared root on a staging directory it
then RemoveAll'd, with no Forget.

Smaller, same theme: createBlobFromFile read WORKTREE files through
entiredir, binding them to .entire's policy; removeEntireDirectory
guessed cwd for a recursive delete on any WorktreeRoot failure rather
than only on git's positive not-a-repository verdict; the session-state
read path opened a child root with no symlink check, which
osroot.OpenChild now performs; and settings.readConfinedIn was a second
copy of osroot.OpenNoFollow.

The external-agent discovery tests built a fake .git directory and leaned
on settings.Load falling back to a cwd-relative path when the anchor
failed. That fallback is gone, so they name the worktree root in the
context instead. One of them was passing for the wrong reason: a disabled
setting and an unreadable one both end at IsExternalAgentsEnabled

8057a0ef9 2026-09-01T11:52:42+01:00 Anchor every os.Root on a trusted base
An os.Root is only as trustworthy as the directory it is opened on, and the
wrong version of that reads as the right one:

    root, _ := osroot.Shared(filepath.Dir(target))
    data, _ := osroot.ReadFile(root, filepath.Base(target))

Every component the caller resolved sits ABOVE that root, so the containment
covers one fixed name and enforces nothing the filepath.Join had not already
decided. A symlink at .claude, at .entire, at entire-investigations is
resolved before the root exists. Anchoring one level up -- on a directory a
resolver produced -- makes those components names INSIDE the root, which is
what os.Root and MkdirAllNoSymlink can refuse.

Three call sites shipped the derived-base shape, and one of them had a
containment check that could never fire: settings.clonePreferencesRoot
computed its common dir as filepath.Dir(filepath.Dir(abs)) and handed both
to gitdir.OpenPathIn, so the relative path was correct by construction. It
now recovers the common dir by removing a compile-time constant suffix,
which fails loudly on a path of the wrong shape. contexts and discovery take
the DIRECTORY the caller chose instead of the file: configRoot(configDir),
and a cacheFile{dir, name} pair in place of a joined path.

Two roots stay anchored on their target's parent and now say why: tokenstore
($ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE_PATH) and settings' explicit-path fallback both act on
a path the CALLER named, so its parent is the caller's choice too and there
is no separate trusted base to prefer.

The seven agent hook-config trees had no root at all. Each of .claude,
.cursor, .gemini, .github/hooks, .factory, .codex and .opencode/plugin was
four lines of filepath.Join + os.MkdirAll + os.WriteFile carrying a
//nolint:gosec saying the path came from the repo root -- which describes
where the path was BUILT, not where it RESOLVES. A working tree arrives by
clone, so a repository carrying a checked-in symlink at .claude had `entire
enable` create directories and write JSON through it, outside the repository
included. agent.HookConfigFile replaces all seven with one type anchored on
the worktree root.

One behaviour change falls out of that and is pinned by a test rather than
left to be discovered: an ABSOLUTE symlink at the config FILE
(.claude/settings.json -> ~/dotfiles/...) no longer resolves, because
os.Root refuses absolute symlinks unconditionally. A relative link inside
the worktree still works, and a symlinked config DIRECTORY is now refused --
which is the point.

investigate gets the same treatment, and there it covers a sink its own
comments already warned about: StateStore.RunDir noted that an unvalidated
run id "would be a path-traversal sink" because callers feed the result to
os.RemoveAll, and clean did exactly that with two functions returning
absolute paths. Deleting now belongs to the stores, which resolve a run id
as a name inside the git common dir. Reading gets it too, closing a real
gap: LocalManifest.FindingsDoc is an absolute path decoded from a JSON file
on disk, and show plus the run footer both followed it, so a manifest could
choose which file was printed. Bootstrap no longer writes at all -- it
renders a body the caller persists through StateStore.WriteFindings.

Also rooted: the checkpoint loose-object delete; the trail worktree
checkout's .gitignore and .worktreeinclude, plus the SOURCE half of its
ignored-file copy (the destination was already rooted on the argument that
the branch content is not user-authored -- the same argument applies to the
files being read); the plugin asset download; the hook-path attribution
read, which read every file in `git status` output on a joined path; the
trail-review location reads, which went through a hand-rolled validator and
take their path from the API; and rewind's restore, which kept a
`repoRoot = "."` fallback and its own os.OpenRoot. Restoring a checkpoint
tree into whatever directory the process is sitting in is worse than not
restoring; it now fails, goes through worktreedir, and creates directories
with MkdirAllNoSymlink, which matters most there because the tree entries
may have been fetched from a remote.

agent.sessionStoreForWrite had the inverse problem: a SessionRef outside the
agent's session store fell through to a root anchored on its own parent, so
the one input that failed the containment check was the one input that
disabled it. The comment justifying that said some agents resolve a restored

The read-only audit found two confirmed resolver-to-write traversal defects: Kilo and Grok. The other eight adapters contain or reject slash-based traversal. Current CLI validation blocks the demonstrated payloads, but adapter APIs remain unsafe outside that specific call path.

The worktrees stayed clean. All eight Go module suites pass. The checked external-agents `HEAD` and `origin/main` remain `887356f`; CLI `HEAD` and `origin/main` are now both `171a7df`, so the earlier `8a43e78` public-main observation is stale.

| Agent | Session ID → path | Hook-generated `SessionRef` | `write-session` | Relevant coverage / result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Amp | Sanitizes unsafe characters and appends extension in `agents/entire-agent-amp/internal/amp/paths.go:14-28`. | Uses the sanitized resolver in `hooks.go:45-59,317-326`. | Writes the supplied ref directly, `transcript.go:168-175`. | Hostile resolver cases and hook sanitization exist in `paths_test.go:17-35`; benign write coverage. Contained. |
| Kiro | Sanitizes unsafe characters in `agents/entire-agent-kiro/internal/kiro/paths.go:14-28`. | Capture/ref paths use the safe resolver in `hooks.go:101-129` and `transcript.go:514-563`. | Trusts supplied ref in `agent.go:93-101`. | Hostile resolver and IDE traversal cases in `paths_test.go:30-48`; contained. |
| Goose | Explicitly rejects separators, colon, NUL, dot IDs in `agents/entire-agent-goose/internal/goose/paths.go:39-60`. | Hook path creation follows validation, `hooks.go:53-70,96-115`. | Trusts supplied ref in `transcript.go:150-157`. | Resolver, hook, and export traversal regressions exist in `paths_test.go:17-56`; contained. |
| OMP | Strict allowlist plus `.`/`..` rejection in `agents/entire-agent-omp/internal/omp/paths.go:241-283`. | Rejects unsafe hook IDs and checks snapshot containment in `hooks.go:61-143,202-267`. | Direct ref write in `transcript.go:56-82`. | Unsafe-ID coverage in `paths_test.go:231-237` and `hooks_test.go:167+`; contained. |
| Qwen | Uses `safeFilename`, `agents/entire-agent-qwen/internal/qwen/agent.go:84-92`. | Hook/sidecar uses sanitized naming, `hooks.go:24-36`, `transcript.go:274-326`. | Direct ref write in `transcript.go:80-87`. | Shared benign test only; no focused hostile resolver test. Contained by inspection/probe. |
| Hermes | Slug plus hash under its transcript root, `agents/entire-agent-hermes/internal/hermes/agent.go:89-113`. | Safe ref emitted by `agent.go:199-236`. | The sole adapter that verifies ownership/containment before writing, `agent.go:152-163`, `transcript.go:251-298`. | Unsafe/collision resolver coverage at `agent_test.go:111-140`; outside write rejection at `agent_test.go:850+`. Contained. |
| Kilo | **Unsafe:** public resolver delegates to raw `filepath.Join(sessionDir, sessionID+".json")`, `agents/entire-agent-kilo/internal/kilo/paths.go:5-10`, `internal/protocol/protocol.go:357-362`. | Hook transcript path already applies `safeSessionID`, `hooks.go:62-126,546-555`. Pre-validation turn writes use that safe path. | Direct ref write in `transcript.go:116-123`. | No hostile public-resolver test. `../outside` was reproduced outside the requested directory and then written through `WriteSession`. |
| Grok | **Unsafe:** raw ID is a directory component in both public and native resolvers, `agents/entire-agent-grok/internal/grok/agent.go:70-81`, `paths.go:133-145`. | `ParseHook` returns the raw-ID native ref, `hooks.go:21-35`; its pre-return marker alone uses safe naming, `transcript.go:276-323`. | Creates directories and writes transcript/summary directly, `transcript.go:81-100`. | `paths_test.go:17-25` covers only benign paths. `../outside` resolver and write escape reproduced. |
| CrewAI | Python `entire-adapter` replaces slash/backslash before forming the filename. | Package hook emits the package resolver result. | Wrapper trusts any nonempty string ref, `protocol_wrapper.py:74-112`. | Wrapper tests cover types/base64 and benign roundtrip, not hostile IDs. Separator traversal contained. Windows drive-relative defect remains below. |
| LangGraph | Same `entire-adapter` path behavior as CrewAI. | Same package hook behavior. | Same direct ref behavior. | Same coverage gap. Separator traversal contained. |

Seven Go protocol copies expose the unsafe generic helper: Amp, Kiro, Goose, OMP, Qwen, Kilo, and Grok. Only Kilo calls it in production. Kiro’s `internal/protocol/handlers_test.go:23-24` calls it as a test helper; the remaining copies appear dead. This is a confirmed maintenance hazard, while Kilo is the confirmed deployed defect.

Current CLI mitigations are substantial:

- `cmd/entire/cli/validation/validators.go:20-53` rejects slash, backslash, colon, absolute paths, volume names, globs, leading dash, NUL-relevant invalid forms, and exact `.`/`..`.
- Restore validates first in `cmd/entire/cli/transcript.go:18-46`; the multi-session path also validates in `strategy/manual_commit_pending.go:380-419`.
- `agent/session_store.go:125-160` performs lexical containment, and writes at `:176-192` use `os.Root`.
- The existing restore regression at `resume_test.go:928-1002` rejects `../victim/secret`.
- Central lifecycle dispatch validates after `ParseHook`, so current CLI use rejects Grok’s returned `../` ID. Grok’s earlier marker write is safely named. Kilo’s pre-validation hook write also uses its safe transcript path.

Those protections do not wrap writes made inside an external-agent subprocess. `agent/external/external.go:175-185,204-213` passes the ref to the adapter, which then calls normal OS file APIs. Direct `write-session` generally trusts the protocol caller’s supplied path; by itself this does not grant a caller new privileges, but it makes unsafe resolver output immediately actionable.

The pinned `external-agents-tests` revision is `3220ca8cc7ba2fbfc5a951ce4a5937ca1a5ca26e`, pinned at `.github/workflows/protocol-compliance.yml:71-78`. Its resolver test uses only `test-session-123` and checks nonempty/path-contains-ID at `tests/mandatory/protocol_test.go:78-90`. The session roundtrip at `tests/mandatory/session_test.go:13-79` likewise uses a benign ID. It has no containment invariant, hostile IDs, hook-path security checks, or Windows job. The repository workflow runs the ten adapters on Ubuntu only.

The Python package has a separate confirmed construction defect. `entire_adapter/utils.py:216-220` replaces separators but does not neutralize Windows drive-relative IDs. With a `PureWindowsPath` base of `C:\sessions`, `D:outside` produces `D:outside.jsonl`, dropping the base. CLI colon rejection mitigates current dispatch. The upstream `entire-adapter` main at `0884561f` still identifies as 0.2.2 and retains this code. Its `TranscriptWriter.append`, `utils.py:243-254`, writes before CLI hook validation, so fixing only the external repository wrapper would be incomplete.

The reported Windows `".. "` escape remains a hypothesis. CLI currently accepts IDs with trailing spaces/dots and Windows device names. Win32 commonly strips terminal spaces/dots, while Grok uses the ID as a directory component and writes with `os.MkdirAll`/`os.WriteFile`; that combination may turn `".. "` into a parent reference. macOS preserves it as a literal child directory. Go’s Windows `os.Root` uses handle-relative operations, but Grok’s subprocess writes bypass `os.Root`. This needs a real Windows proof before being described as exploitable. Names such as `CON`, `NUL`, and `COM1` are portability and reliability concerns and should remain advisory unless a stronger impact is demonstrated.

I recommend this sequence:

1. **Own the cross-agent contract in `entireio/external-agents-tests`.** Extend `tests/mandatory/protocol_test.go` with hostile IDs including `../escape`, `..`, nested traversal, backslashes, drive forms, and `".. "`. An adapter may reject or sanitize, but any successful nonempty result must be proven inside the requested directory using `filepath.Rel`, not string-prefix matching. Add a resolver→write sentinel test using only the returned ref. Add a targeted Windows job.

2. **Fix Kilo test-first in external-agents.** Add hostile public-resolver and resolver→write tests under `agents/entire-agent-kilo/internal/kilo`. Make the public resolver reuse the same `safeSessionID` mapping as the hook so discovery, hook refs, and restore agree. Preserve the existing native filename/layout.

3. **Fix Grok test-first.** Add hostile tests for the public resolver, native resolver, hook output, and resolver→write chain. Because real Grok IDs are generated in a constrained format, validate and reject unexpected IDs before computing native paths or writing the marker. Reuse one validator in `ResolveSessionFile`, `nativeTranscriptPath`/`resolveSessionRef`, and `ParseHook`.

4. **Remove the generic raw helper from all seven protocol copies.** Path layout belongs to each adapter. Replace Kiro’s test-only call with a fixed safe ref or local stub. Removal eliminates the latent footgun without inventing one generic sanitization policy that may disagree with native layouts.

5. **Fill local gaps.** Add focused hostile resolver tests for Qwen and the Python wrappers. Add hook assertions where coverage currently verifies only benign paths. Avoid requiring every `write-session` implementation to confine an arbitrary caller-provided ref unless the protocol contract is intentionally changed; test the resolver-produced chain instead.

6. **Fix and release `entire-adapter`.** Make the resolved transcript name a single safe component, preferably with a stable short hash when normalization changes the ID to avoid collisions. Add slash, backslash, colon, dot, edge-space/dot, collision, and `PureWindowsPath` drive-relative tests, including `TranscriptWriter`’s hook ref. Release 0.2.3, then bump both agents’ pins and their build-task expectations/documentation.

7. **Harden CLI ID validation separately.** In `validation/validators.go`, reject surrounding whitespace, terminal dots, control characters, and Windows reserved device basenames. Extend `validators_test.go` and the restore no-write regression. A second validation at the external `WriteSession` sink is reasonable defense in depth if the request still carries the original session ID.

8. **Do not change `paths.IsRelativeTraversal`.** Its current job at `paths/paths.go:317-321` is lexical relative-path detection and it is used broadly for checkpoint, git, worktree, and store paths. Teaching it Win32 trailing-space normalization would conflate opaque identifier policy with filesystem traversal and change legitimate POSIX semantics. Put portable ID rules in `ValidateSessionID`; add a narrowly named Windows-component check at a filesystem boundary only if further proof shows it is needed.

Final validation should include all eight Go modules, both Python adapter suites, shared compliance against all ten binaries, focused CLI validator/restore/SessionStore tests, repository lifecycle E2E, and the targeted Windows regression. The Windows result should determine whether `".. "` is promoted from hypothesis to confirmed defect.

Sol’s independent audit agrees on the core result and found one important distinction: **Kiro is already protected; Kilo is the affected similarly named agent.** It also confirmed that seven copied protocol packages retain the unsafe raw helper, even though only Kilo calls it in production.

I’m doing the final consistency pass on current branch tips and the proposed Windows/CLI boundary before I hand over the plan.

   298	func safeFilename(name string) string {
   299		name = strings.TrimSpace(name)
   300		if name == "" {

   303		var b strings.Builder
   304		for _, r := range name {

   306			case r == '-' || r == '_' || r == '.':
   307				b.WriteRune(r)
   308			case r >= '0' && r <= '9':
   309				b.WriteRune(r)
   310			case r >= 'a' && r <= 'z':
   311				b.WriteRune(r)
   312			case r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z':
   313				b.WriteRune(r)
   314			default:
   315				if unicode.IsLetter(r) || unicode.IsNumber(r) {
   316					b.WriteRune(r)
   317				} else {
   318					b.WriteByte('_')
   319				}
   320			}
   321		}
   322		out := strings.Trim(b.String(), "._")
   323		if out == "" {
   324			return stubSessionID
   325		}

    51	func DispatchLifecycleEvent(ctx context.Context, ag agent.Agent, event *agent.Event) error {
    52		if ag == nil {
    53			return errors.New("agent cannot be nil")

    60		// build filesystem paths. Handlers historically validated individually,
    61		// which is fragile — handleLifecycleTurnEnd builds .entire/metadata/<id>/
    62		// via os.MkdirAll + os.WriteFile, and handleLifecycleSubagentEnd builds a
    63		// subagent transcript path from SubagentID and reads it, without their own
    64		// checks. Centralizing the guard covers every handler (and any future one)
    65		// uniformly. Empty IDs pass through: handlers apply their own empty-handling
    66		// (e.g. TurnEnd falls back to a safe constant; SubagentEnd skips the path).
    67		if event.SessionID != "" {
    68			if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(event.SessionID); err != nil {
    69				return fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID in %s event: %w", event.Type, err)
    70			}
    71		}
    72		if event.ToolUseID != "" {
    73			if err := validation.ValidateToolUseID(event.ToolUseID); err != nil {
    74				return fmt.Errorf("invalid tool use ID in %s event: %w", event.Type, err)
    75			}
    76		}
    77		if event.SubagentID != "" {
    78			if err := validation.ValidateAgentID(event.SubagentID); err != nil {
    79				return fmt.Errorf("invalid subagent ID in %s event: %w", event.Type, err)

    17	// Computes the path dynamically from the current repo location for cross-machine portability.
    18	func resolveTranscriptPath(ctx context.Context, sessionID string, agent agentpkg.Agent) (string, error) {
    19		// Session IDs reaching this restore path can originate from checkpoint
    20		// metadata on the shared entire/checkpoints/v1 branch, which is attacker-

content.text:
We got the following security report, which I am pasting below. Read it but hold any planning and implementation as the author sent a second email afterwards:
1. DESCRIPTION
--------------

In the entireio/external-agents repository, Agent.ResolveSessionFile takes a
session id and returns the path of the session file. Six of the eight Go
agents either sanitize that id or reject an unsafe one. Two do not:

  * entire-agent-kilo: Agent.ResolveSessionFile in internal/kilo/paths.go
    delegates to protocol.ResolveSessionFile in internal/protocol/protocol.go,
    which is filepath.Join(sessionDir, sessionID+".json") on the raw id.

  * entire-agent-grok: Agent.ResolveSessionFile in internal/grok/agent.go
    builds filepath.Join(sessionDir, sessionID, nativeTranscriptFile), placing
    the raw id in as a DIRECTORY segment, guarded only by a check that the id
    is not whitespace.

Because filepath.Join cleans the result, an id containing "../" resolves
upward and the returned path leaves the session directory.

This is the same class PR #58 (fe86948, "amp, kiro: sanitize session paths")
fixed in amp and kiro. That PR scoped itself to those two agents, and the
class was not swept across the other six.

Worth noting: grok already contains a suitable helper. safeFilename in
internal/grok/transcript.go is byte-identical to qwen's, and qwen calls it
from its ResolveSessionFile. Grok's ResolveSessionFile does not.


2. IMPACT
---------

The escaped path is not only returned over the protocol. Both agents write
to it:

  * kilo: atomicWriteFile(session.SessionRef, ...) in Agent.WriteSession
    (internal/kilo/transcript.go) and atomicWriteFile(sessionRef, ...) in
    persistTurnMessages (internal/kilo/hooks.go).

  * grok: os.WriteFile(session.SessionRef, ...) in Agent.WriteSession
    (internal/grok/transcript.go).

So a session id that escapes the session directory becomes a file write at an
attacker-chosen path with attacker-influenced content, at mode 0600, creating
parent directories as needed. I verified the write itself, not merely the
returned string: a probe confined to a scratch worktree ran both binaries and
confirmed the file was created outside the nominated session directory with
the supplied content.

What I did NOT establish is who controls the session id in practice. See
section 6.


3. STEPS TO REPRODUCE
---------------------

At commit 887356f06f517aa2f086140bcf22f91541df69ca of
github.com/entireio/external-agents, working tree clean:

    for a in amp kiro goose omp qwen hermes kilo grok; do
      (cd agents/entire-agent-$a && go build -o /tmp/bin/entire-agent-$a ./cmd/...)
    done

    for a in amp kiro goose omp qwen hermes kilo grok; do
      printf '%-8s ' "$a"
      /tmp/bin/entire-agent-$a resolve-session-file \
        --session-dir /home/u/.entire/sessions \
        --session-id '../../../../tmp/pwned'
    done

Observed:

    amp      {"session_file":"/home/u/.entire/sessions/.._.._.._.._tmp_pwned.json"}
    kiro     {"session_file":"/home/u/.entire/sessions/.._.._.._.._tmp_pwned.json"}
    goose    {"session_file":""}
    omp      {"session_file":""}
    qwen     {"session_file":"/home/u/.entire/sessions/tmp_pwned.jsonl"}
    hermes   {"session_file":"/home/u/.entire/sessions/tmp-pwned-373554abc66c60f6.jsonl"}
    kilo     {"session_file":"/tmp/pwned.json"}
    grok     {"session_file":"/tmp/pwned/chat_history.jsonl"}

kilo and grok escape --session-dir. The other six contain or reject. A benign
id behaves identically across all eight, so a fix is not a behaviour change
for valid input.

Feeding the escaped path back through write-session produces the file at that
location. I can supply that probe script if useful.


4. AFFECTED VERSIONS
--------------------

The repository carries no tags, so I am citing commits.

  * Verified at 887356f06f517aa2f086140bcf22f91541df69ca (2026-09-10), tip of
    main at the time of testing.
  * kilo: present since the agent was added, 2552110 (2026-05-22).
  * grok: present since 760f6fe (2026-07-01).

I have not checked released binaries, only a build from source at that commit.


5. SUGGESTED FIX
----------------

Both have an in-repo precedent, so neither needs new design:

  * kilo: replace the delegation with amp's shape,
    filepath.Join(sessionDir, safePathSessionID(sessionID)+".json"), carrying
    safePathSessionID and its regexp across from
    entire-agent-amp/internal/amp/paths.go.

  * grok: call the safeFilename it already has, as qwen does. Note grok's id
    is a directory segment rather than a filename stem, so sanitizing the
    segment is necessary but please confirm it is sufficient for that shape.

Two related observations from the same sweep, neither of them a vulnerability
today:

  * Neither module has a test that would catch a regression here. A mutation
    run replacing both ResolveSessionFile bodies with `return ""` left both
    module suites reporting ok. kilo has no paths_test.go at all, and grok's
    contains only TestEncodeRepoCWD and TestNativeTranscriptPath. The
    equivalent mutation is caught in amp, kiro, goose, omp and hermes by their
    existing traversal tests.

  * qwen sanitizes correctly today, but its suite does not cover safeFilename,
    so a future weakening there would also go unnoticed.


6. ROUTING NOTE, AND WHAT I COULD NOT ASSESS
--------------------------------------------

Your SECURITY.md reserves advisories for issues exploitable by "a remote or
non-local actor", and treats issues that "cannot be exploited without direct
access to the user's machine" as ordinary bugs. I cannot answer that test from
this repository alone.

Everything above is verified inside entireio/external-agents. What decides
severity is where --session-id comes from, which lives in entireio/cli and
which I have not read. If a session id can be influenced by repository
content, a crafted agent session file, or anything else delivered without
local access, this is a remotely triggered arbitrary file write. If the id
only ever originates from a locally installed agent's own metadata, your
policy says this belongs in GitHub Issues as a bug.

I am sending it here rather than filing publicly because that call is yours,
and because the public route is not reversible if the answer turns out to be
the first one. If you would rather it were a public issue, tell me and I will
open one, or you are welcome to open it yourself.

Also out of scope for me: entireio/external-agents-tests is not vendored in
the repository, so I could not check whether the shared protocol compliance
suite already covers traversal. If it does, kilo and grok should presumably be
failing it.

Happy to provide the probe scripts, the full per-agent output, or the mutation
ledger. I am not planning to disclose this anywhere while you look at it.

Here's part 2:
Follow-up to my report of earlier today. I have since read entireio/cli, which
I had not read when I wrote that mail. Three updates, and the first one LOWERS
the severity I reported. I would rather correct that promptly than leave an
overstated report sitting in your queue.


1. THE PRACTICAL SEVERITY IS LOWER THAN MY REPORT IMPLIED
---------------------------------------------------------

My section 6 said I could not tell whether the traversal was reachable. It
largely is not, because you already block it, and the block is in the CLI
rather than in the agents.

validation.ValidateSessionID in cmd/entire/cli/validation/validators.go
rejects any id containing "/" or "\\". So the exact input in my section 3,
"../../../../tmp/pwned", cannot reach kilo or grok through any caller that
validates. Because separators are rejected, the id is always a single path
component, and filepath.Join cannot escape a single component.

I checked the paths that consume checkpoint metadata off the shared
entire/checkpoints/v1 branch, since that data crosses machines on a fetch and
looked like the obvious remote vector. Both validate before resolving:
RestoreLogsOnly and classifySessionsForRestore, in
cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_pending.go.

So on Linux and macOS I can show no input that escapes through those paths.
Treat my report as: a real unsanitized-id defect in two agent binaries,
currently mitigated by a validator living in a different repository.


2. THE COMPLIANCE-SUITE QUESTION IS NOW ANSWERED
------------------------------------------------

I said I could not check whether entireio/external-agents-tests covers
traversal. I have now read it, and it does not.

The only coverage is TestResolveSessionFile in tests/mandatory/protocol_test.go,
which passes the single benign id "test-session-123" and asserts the returned
session_file contains it. Searching every file in that repository for "../",
"traversal", "sanitiz", "escape" and "outside", the only hits are relative
paths in README examples.

So kilo and grok pass the shared compliance suite today. My "they should
presumably be failing it" was wrong. Usefully, this also means the fix I
suggested will not break compliance: amp's safePathSessionID leaves a benign
id unchanged.


3. A NEW DEFECT, IN entireio/cli, THAT WOULD REOPEN THE GROK CASE
------------------------------------------------------------------

Since your whole defence rests on one validator, the validator is worth
looking at closely. It has an inconsistency.

ValidateSessionID checks emptiness with TrimSpace, but compares the reserved
segment WITHOUT trimming:

    if strings.TrimSpace(id) == "" { ... }      // trims
    if id == "." || id == ".." { ... }          // does not

So the id ".. " (dot, dot, trailing space) passes every clause: it is not
empty, has no separator, is not equal to "..", has no colon, no glob
characters, and is not absolute.

It also passes your containment check. Go's filepath.Clean treats ".. " as an
ordinary name, so filepath.Rel yields ".. /transcript", and
paths.IsRelativeTraversal in cmd/entire/cli/paths/paths.go matches only "..",
"../" and "..\\", none of which is a prefix of ".. /".

Demonstrated with the two functions reimplemented standalone, grok's shape:

    id="ok-123"  validator=true   traversal_flagged=false
      -> /home/u/.entire/sessions/ok-123/chat_history.jsonl
    id=".."      validator=false  traversal_flagged=true
      -> /home/u/.entire/chat_history.jsonl
    id=".. "     validator=true   traversal_flagged=false
      -> /home/u/.entire/sessions/.. /chat_history.jsonl

On Linux and macOS that last line is inert: it creates a directory literally
named ".. " and escapes nothing.

UNVERIFIED, AND I AM NOT ASSERTING IT: Win32 strips trailing spaces and dots
from path components. If that normalisation applies to the write grok performs,
the component becomes ".." and the write lands one directory above the session
directory, having passed both the validator and the containment check. I have
no Windows machine to test this on and I will not claim it without a run. Go
switches to the \\?\ extended-length form for long paths, which disables the
stripping, so it may not hold even there.

The asymmetry that makes this agent-specific: built-in agents write through
SessionStore.WriteFile using an *os.Root with handle-relative opens, which do
not apply Win32 normalisation. An external agent does its own write inside
write-session. And it only bites a resolver that uses the id as a DIRECTORY
component, which is grok and not kilo.

The blocking artifact is one test on Windows: what does os.WriteFile do with a
path containing a ".. " component.

TestValidateSessionID in validators_test.go has cases named "single dot",
"double dot", "path traversal attempt", "absolute windows path" and
"whitespace-only session ID", but none for dot-dot with adjacent whitespace.
It reads as untested rather than deliberately allowed.

Two fixes that close it without anyone having to settle the Win32 question:
trim before the reserved-segment comparison, and teach IsRelativeTraversal to
recognise a component that normalises to "..".


4. ONE OBSERVATION ABOUT THE SHAPE OF THE DEFENCE
--------------------------------------------------

Your own comment above the validation call in manual_commit_pending.go says
the session ID "is attacker-influenceable" and that rejecting separators stops
a crafted ID that "would otherwise let a crafted session ID overwrite files
outside the agent session directory". The SECURITY CONTRACT comment on
Agent.ResolveSessionFile in cmd/entire/cli/agent/agent.go says the same, and
notes that "some implementations use it as a directory component", which
describes grok exactly.

So the analysis is already correct in your codebase. The observation is only
that it is enforced in one place, in a different repository from the binaries
it protects, against agents you do not control, with no defence in depth
behind it. That is why a whitespace inconsistency in one function is worth
more attention than it would otherwise be, and why I would still fix kilo and
grok even though the validator currently covers them.

Nothing here changes my routing question in section 6 of the original mail, or
my undertaking not to disclose while you look at it.
Run investigation and planning. Make sure to cover all agents supported by this repo, but not just Kiro and Grok.
Continue with Sol then

# Entire Adapter

Python adapter that lets LangGraph/LangChain and CrewAI agents participate in Entire checkpoint tracking.

It provides:

- `EntireCallbackHandler` for LangChain and LangGraph callback configs.
- `EntireCrewAIListener` for CrewAI's event bus.
- Three Entire external-agent binaries:
  - `entire-agent-langgraph`
  - `entire-agent-crewai`
  - `entire-agent-entire-adapter` for backward-compatible generic use.

## Why

Custom Python agents often edit files through tools, but their prompt/tool context is easy to lose once the final Git diff lands. Entire Adapter maps framework lifecycle events to Entire hooks so commits can be linked to agent sessions, tool calls, and checkpoint history.

## Install

For LangGraph/LangChain:

```bash
pip install "entire-adapter[langgraph]"
entire enable --agent langgraph --telemetry=false
```

For CrewAI:

```bash
pip install "entire-adapter[crewai]"
entire enable --agent crewai --telemetry=false

# Security Policy

We take security seriously at Entire. We appreciate your efforts to responsibly disclose vulnerabilities and will make every effort to acknowledge your contributions.

## Reporting a Vulnerability

**Please do not report security vulnerabilities through public GitHub issues.**

Instead, please send security-related reports to **[security@entire.io](mailto:security@entire.io)**.

### What to Include

When reporting a vulnerability, please include:

1. **Description** - A clear description of the vulnerability
2. **Impact** - What an attacker could achieve by exploiting this issue
3. **Steps to reproduce** - Detailed steps to reproduce the vulnerability
4. **Affected versions** - Which versions of the CLI are affected (if known)
5. **Suggested fix** - If you have ideas on how to fix it (optional)

### What to Expect

- **Acknowledgment** - We will acknowledge receipt of your report within 48 hours
- **Updates** - We will keep you informed of our progress as we investigate
- **Resolution** - We aim to resolve critical vulnerabilities within 90 days

## Confidentiality

**All reports will be kept confidential.** We will not share your information with third parties without your consent, except as required by law.

## Supported Versions

We recommend always running the latest version of the Entire CLI.

## Scope

This security policy applies to:

- The Entire CLI (`entire` command-line tool)
- Official Entire GitHub repositories
- Entire-related services at entire.com or entire.io

### Out of Scope

The following are generally not considered security vulnerabilities:

- Issues in third-party dependencies (please report these upstream)
- Social engineering attacks
- Denial of service attacks
- Issues requiring physical access to a user's device

---

## Security Advisories

Security advisories are issued when a confirmed vulnerability can be exploited by a remote or non-local actor. Because the Entire CLI is primarily used as a local development tool, the following are generally treated as **bug reports rather than security advisories**:

- Regular expression performance issues (ReDoS) that only affect local execution
- Resource exhaustion that requires local access to trigger
- Issues that cannot be exploited without direct access to the user's machine

Use GitHub Issues for the respective repository to report bugs.

---

Thank you for helping keep Entire and our community safe!

57b275ac6 2026-09-01T11:52:52+01:00 agent: reject volume-relative paths in SessionStore.Name
Cursor Bugbot, session_store.go:146 (High). Not in the trail findings.

Name gated only on filepath.IsAbs, so a Windows drive-relative path such as
"C:foo" — separator-free, and reported non-absolute — was accepted as a name
inside the store, while filepath.Join drops the base directory when the
appended element carries a volume. SessionFile then handed that escaped path
back as absPath.

validation.ValidateSessionID already rejects this shape, and its comment
describes the same mechanism, so the reachable paths are covered today. But
SessionStore is the containment layer this branch introduces — Name exists to
answer "is this inside the store?" independently of whether a caller
remembered to validate — and it was the one place pairing IsAbs with nothing.
The other three (ValidateSessionID, alternates_fs, alternates_rewrite) all
pair it with VolumeName.

Route a volumed path down the absolute branch so filepath.Rel rejects it
across volumes. No-op on Unix, where VolumeName is always empty.

Not verified on Windows hardware: the change is inert on this platform, and
CI's Windows leg only runs tests matching (Windows|MSYS).

83677f751 2026-09-01T11:52:47+01:00 Pin every path component instead of checking it and looking again
NoSymlinkedParent walked a name's parents with Lstat and then handed the
WHOLE name back to the original root, so the thing that was checked and
the thing that was opened were resolved twice, independently. Everything
in this package now opens each component in turn, keeps the descriptor,
and operates relative to it: OpenDirNoSymlinks descends one component at
a time, OpenParentNoSymlinks pins the parent and returns the leaf, and
ReadFileNoFollow, OpenFileNoFollow, LstatNoSymlinks, RemoveNoSymlinks,
ReadDirNoSymlinks and WalkDirNoSymlinks are all expressed on top of that
pair. NoSymlinkedParent survives as a predicate and now says in its own
doc that a caller acting on the result must re-open through
OpenParentNoSymlinks rather than trust it.

MkdirAllNoSymlink follows the same rule for the directories it creates,
so a component that appears between the check and the Mkdir is opened
and identity-checked like any other rather than being MkdirAll'd blind.
OpenChild stops reporting a regular file as ErrSymlinkedPath and returns
ErrWalkRootNotDirectory: replacing a link and replacing a file are
different remedies.

The atomic writers no longer fsync. The rename is what gives every
caller here the property it actually needs, that a reader never sees a
torn file; fsync buys durability across a power loss, and nothing
written through these functions is worth that — settings, session state,
caches and manifests are all reconstructible. It is not free either,
measured at 14x on a 4KiB payload (1.02ms against 71µs) with session
state written on every agent hook. What is surrendered is stated in the
doc rather than left implicit.

Writing atomically into an agent's config directory does leave a temp
file beside the target if the process dies between the create and the
rename. The window is now a few tens of microseconds and only `enable`
and `trail checkout` can open it, but the result is permanent, and
Entire diffs untracked files across a turn — so a months-old
.claude/settings.json.<hex>.tmp gets captured into the next checkpoint
as a file that turn created. `entire clean --all` now sweeps them. The
capture path deliberately does NOT learn to ignore them: the worktree
belongs to the user, and silently dropping a file from their checkpoint
is worse than the stray it would hide.

HookConfigFile now refuses a symlinked leaf as well as a symlinked
parent, reversing an earlier decision in this branch. The reason is
recorded where the policy is: the merge read pulls the link target's
contents into what Entire writes, and the write is a rename, so it
replaces the user's link with a regular file rather than following it.
Both are silent. A deliberately symlinked settings.json still works by
keeping it out of the index, which is what a dotfile workflow does.

331c7b130 2026-09-01T11:52:44+01:00 Refuse what os.Root only confined
The anchors landed in the previous three commits. This is the tail, and
most of it is one bug wearing several hats: os.Root contains a path
without saying anything about what the path is.

fs.WalkDir takes its walk root's DirEntry from fs.Stat, which follows a
symlink, and only the entries below it from ReadDir, which does not.
Every symlink guard here inspected d.Type() inside the callback, so none
of them covered the root: a symlinked .entire/metadata/<session> was
descended into and its target redacted, committed and pushed.
filepath.Walk lstat'd its root, so this was lost in the conversion, not
absent from the start. osroot.WalkDirNoSymlinks lstats the root and
refuses a symlink at both levels; the two checkpoint metadata walks,
clean's tmp walk and doctor's reporter use it. redact.LoadPacks gets the
same check through fs.ReadLinkFS, which os.Root.FS() implements, so it
keeps its fs.FS-only API and its dependency-free position. A symlinked
.entire is refused rather than followed now, so doctor and CLAUDE.md stop
telling the user that intentional setups keep working.

jsonutil.WriteFileAtomicIn leaves <base>.<16 hex>.tmp beside its target,
and .entire/metadata/<session> is copied wholesale into every checkpoint
tree. A hook killed between the create and the rename left an orphan that
was committed on every checkpoint from then on, and ParseChunkIndex read
it back as a transcript CHUNK: fmt.Sscanf("%03d") stops at the first
non-digit, so full.jsonl.123abc...tmp parsed as chunk 123 and was
reassembled into the transcript. Both walks skip jsonutil.IsTempName, and
a chunk suffix must now be entirely digits.

SessionStore resolved its root through osroot.Shared, a registry that
never evicts. searchTranscriptInProjectDirs opens a store for every
candidate directory it walks under an agent's session base dir, so each
probe retained a directory fd for the life of the process, measured at
one per directory against zero for the os.Stat it replaced. A store is
not a long-lived anchor: it opens a root per operation and closes it
again. plugin_install_remote took a shared root on a staging directory it
then RemoveAll'd, with no Forget.

Smaller, same theme: createBlobFromFile read WORKTREE files through
entiredir, binding them to .entire's policy; removeEntireDirectory
guessed cwd for a recursive delete on any WorktreeRoot failure rather
than only on git's positive not-a-repository verdict; the session-state
read path opened a child root with no symlink check, which
osroot.OpenChild now performs; and settings.readConfinedIn was a second
copy of osroot.OpenNoFollow.

The external-agent discovery tests built a fake .git directory and leaned
on settings.Load falling back to a cwd-relative path when the anchor
failed. That fallback is gone, so they name the worktree root in the
context instead. One of them was passing for the wrong reason: a disabled
setting and an unreadable one both end at IsExternalAgentsEnabled
returning false.
